description: One Arcus service in depth: availability, platform messaging, Cassandra, JVM, thread pools and logs. Arcus Overview compares all services; its panels link here with the service preselected.

panels.title: Alerts
panels.description: Alert rules firing, pending or erroring right now whose instance carries the selected service as its job label. Rules that key on other labels (deployment, container) are on Arcus Overview.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape the service's metrics port on a ready pod.

panels.title: Ready Pods
panels.description: Containers of this service passing their readiness probe.

panels.title: Restarts (24h)
panels.description: Container restarts in the last 24 hours. Any value here means the process exited or was killed; see Last Termination for why.

panels.title: Running For
panels.description: Age of the current container. Red for the first ten minutes after a start, so a fresh restart stands out.

panels.title: Partitions Assigned
panels.description: Platform partitions this instance owns. 0 is a standby: another datacenter holds the partitions (platform-services is a singleton across the fleet). Blank for services that don't partition.

panels.title: Last Termination
panels.description: Why the previous container of this pod stopped. OOMKilled means the memory limit was hit; Error means the JVM exited non-zero (check the logs around the restart).

panels.title: Up / Down
panels.description: Scrape result over time: a gap or DOWN is a restart, a rollout, or the metrics port not answering.

panels.title: Restarts per Hour
panels.description: Container restarts, per pod, in each hour. Lines up with Last Termination and the logs below.

panels.title: Platform Messages (/s)
panels.description: Messages on the platform bus (Kafka) for this service: read off the topic, received for processing, sent, and discarded as not for this instance. A send-error rate above zero means Kafka rejected writes.

panels.title: Message Timing p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of how long a received message had waited on the bus before this service read it (receive delay), and of the time to send one. Same timer units as the DAO panels.

panels.title: Messages Processed by Type (/s)
panels.description: Platform messages this service handled, by message type (the metric name with the messages_platform_proc_type_ prefix removed). The sum across metric names needs the label_replace and subquery; a plain rate collides on identical label sets.

panels.title: Intra-service Messages (/s)
panels.description: Messages on the intra-service bus (heartbeats, partition traffic between instances).

panels.title: DAO Latency p95
panels.description: 95th percentile Cassandra operation time, slowest DAO per operation type. A step up across every service at once is Cassandra; one service alone is its query pattern.

panels.title: DAO Throughput (ops/s)
panels.description: Cassandra operations per second by type.

panels.title: Heap Used vs Max
panels.description: Heap in use against -Xmx. Used climbing to max with Old Gen After GC high as well means the service is short of heap, not just between collections.

panels.title: Old Gen After GC (% of max)
panels.description: Old-generation heap still in use after the last collection, as a share of its max: live data the service cannot free. Above 90% for long means it needs more heap. Covers the Serial (Tenured Gen) and G1 (G1 Old Gen) collectors.

targets.expr: max by (job) ({__name__=~"jvm_memory_pools_(Tenured_Gen|G1_Old_Gen)_used_after_gc", job=~"$service"}) / max by (job) ({__name__=~"jvm_memory_pools_(Tenured_Gen|G1_Old_Gen)_max", job=~"$service"})

panels.title: Non-Heap (Metaspace) Used
panels.description: Memory outside the heap: class metadata, code cache. Grows with loaded classes; a steady climb is a class-loader leak.

panels.title: GC Rate (/s)
panels.description: Collections per second by collector, whichever collector the JVM runs (Serial: Copy and MarkSweepCompact; G1: Young and Old Generation).

panels.title: GC Time (ms/s)
panels.description: Milliseconds per second spent in garbage collection, by collector. Sustained time in the old-generation collector is the service running out of heap.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: Live JVM threads, with the blocked and deadlocked counts. Deadlocked above zero is a stuck service even if it still answers probes.

panels.title: Pool Tasks Running
panels.description: Tasks executing right now in each executor pool.

panels.title: Pool Tasks Queued
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a thread. A queue that grows and doesn't drain is a pool too small for its load, or work stuck behind a slow dependency.

panels.title: Pool Tasks Failed (/s)
panels.description: Tasks that ended in an exception, per pool. Pair with Error Logs below.

panels.title: Pool Enqueue Time p95
panels.description: How long a task waited in the queue before a thread picked it up, 95th percentile, per pool. Same timer units as the DAO panels.

panels.title: Pool Threads
panels.description: Threads alive in each pool.

panels.title: Log Volume by Level (lines/min)
panels.description: Log lines per minute by level, from the level label Alloy sets on every stream. Error and warn climbing while info stays flat is the service hitting a problem; everything climbing is a restart or debug logging left on.

panels.title: ZooKeeper Client Events
panels.description: Session timeouts, expirations and reconnects logged by this service's ZooKeeper client. An expiry makes the service exit (see ZooKeeper Session Expired).

panels.title: Logs
panels.description: Latest log lines for the selected service, filtered by "Search" (case-insensitive regex). Stack traces are joined onto the line that raised them.

list.description: The Arcus services are the only JVMs Prometheus scrapes, so this lists exactly them. Pick more than one to compare.
list.label: Service
list.name: service

list.description: Case-insensitive regex applied to the Logs panel.
